legend: For an integer array b%%ZSMJ0%% and a given integer k%%ZSMJ1%%, define S(b)%%ZSMJ2%% as follows. Perform exactly k%%ZSMJ3%% operations; in each operation, compute the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence∗%%ZSMJ4%% (LIS) of the current array b%%ZSMJ5%% and append this value to the end of b%%ZSMJ6%%. Each operation acts on the array obtained from the previous ones. After the k%%ZSMJ7%% operations, S(b)%%ZSMJ8%% is the sum of all elements of the resulting array.

You are given an integer array a%%ZSMJ9%% of length n%%ZSMJ10%% and the integer k%%ZSMJ11%%. For each i%%ZSMJ12%% from 1%%ZSMJ13%% to n%%ZSMJ14%%, compute S(a[1..i])%%ZSMJ15%%, where a[1..i]%%ZSMJ16%% denotes the prefix a1,a2,…,ai%%ZSMJ17%%. Each prefix is processed independently: the operations performed while computing S(a[1..i])%%ZSMJ18%% do not affect any other prefix.

∗%%ZSMJ19%%A subsequence is obtained from an array by deleting zero or more elements without changing the order of the remaining ones; it is strictly increasing if each of its elements is strictly greater than the previous one.
input: The first line contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ20%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ21%%) — the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case contains two integers n%%ZSMJ22%% and k%%ZSMJ23%% (1≤n≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ24%%, 1≤k≤109%%ZSMJ25%%) — the length of the array and the number of operations.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ26%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ27%% (−109≤ai≤109%%ZSMJ28%%) — the elements of the array.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ29%% over all test cases does not exceed 3⋅105%%ZSMJ30%%.
output: For each test case, output n%%ZSMJ31%% integers on a single line — the values S(a[1..1]),S(a[1..2]),…,S(a[1..n])%%ZSMJ32%%.
note: In the first test case, a=[1,3,0]%%ZSMJ33%% and k=2%%ZSMJ34%%. Each prefix is processed independently.

Prefix [1]%%ZSMJ35%%: the LIS has length 1%%ZSMJ36%%, so we append 1%%ZSMJ37%%, giving [1,1]%%ZSMJ38%%. The LIS is still 1%%ZSMJ39%% (the two equal values 1%%ZSMJ40%% cannot both belong to a strictly increasing subsequence), so we append 1%%ZSMJ41%% again, giving [1,1,1]%%ZSMJ42%%. The sum is 1+1+1=3%%ZSMJ43%%.

Prefix [1,3]%%ZSMJ44%%: the LIS has length 2%%ZSMJ45%%, so we append 2%%ZSMJ46%%, giving [1,3,2]%%ZSMJ47%%. The LIS is still 2%%ZSMJ48%%, so we append 2%%ZSMJ49%% again, giving [1,3,2,2]%%ZSMJ50%%. The sum is 1+3+2+2=8%%ZSMJ51%%.

Prefix [1,3,0]%%ZSMJ52%%: the LIS has length 2%%ZSMJ53%%, so we append 2%%ZSMJ54%%, giving [1,3,0,2]%%ZSMJ55%%. The LIS is still 2%%ZSMJ56%%, so we append 2%%ZSMJ57%% again, giving [1,3,0,2,2]%%ZSMJ58%%. The sum is 1+3+0+2+2=8%%ZSMJ59%%.
So the answer for the first test case is 3 8 8%%ZSMJ60%%.
